A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research and contain 26 complete pages, including Appendices A–E. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison; pages 3–26 are visually identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original 3DSSG experiments evaluating the proposed model, encoder transfer, component ablations, and weak supervision in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original quantitative and qualitative experiments, including the proposed model's results in Tables 2–14.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same object-encoder pretraining, semantic/geometric relationship encoder, LSE, GSE, BEG, and training objectives. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 3DSSG/3RScan indoor data and object, predicate, triplet, SGCls, and PredCls tasks. The seen/unseen and predicate-frequency evaluations in Appendix D are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within every comparison, including SGPN, SGFN, and VL-SAT; Zhang et al. in Tables 3 and 10; KERN in Table 10; and 3D-VLAP in Table 14. The loss comparators in Table 6 are also retained.

E3.justification: The data split, preprocessing, training budgets, checkpoint selection, metrics, and graph-constraint settings are identical. Appendix C and the evaluation protocols in Appendix D contain no revisions.

E4.justification: The encoder-transfer experiments, loss and component ablations, entropy analysis, feature visualizations, and scene-graph case studies are retained unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B and D.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The unchanged mean-recall and mean-accuracy metrics average across classes rather than quantify run uncertainty.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–14 and the qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports the same proposed-model object R@1 of 59.53, predicate R@1 of 91.27, and triplet R@50 of 91.40 in both versions.

T1.justification: The equations, conditional-sufficiency and posterior-factorization assumptions, and both propositions and proofs in Appendix B are identical. No mathematical reasoning is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about discriminative object features, transferable encoder benefits, relationship modeling, and performance under the closed-vocabulary 3DSSG setting.

C2.justification: Interpretations of object uncertainty, component interactions, and weak-supervision errors are unchanged. Appendix E retains the limitations concerning absent object detection and the requirement for a complete scene without incremental updates.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical software, hardware, hyperparameters, processing instructions, training times, and checkpoint-selection details. The code-access statement and URL are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 64 references and research-positioning discussions are retained, including Appendix A. No cited work or substantive novelty relationship changes.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 29 December 2025 to v3 dated 2 February 2026. The manuscript prose, terminology, headings, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 has revised rendering of the scene thumbnails and embedding graphics, different graph-label typography, and small positioning changes. Its labels, explanatory content, and caption are retained; all other scientific displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 changes only the version/date stamp and Figure 1's graphical presentation. The figure remains readable and conveys the same message in both versions, while the scientific evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and limitations are identical. These cosmetic adjustments leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
